sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Calumet County?
sections.html:
Two layers handle it. Each town, village and city in Calumet County contracts its own assessor and runs its own treasurer, while the Calumet County Treasurer in Chilton takes care of the county side of the work.

The county treasurer is Mike Schlaak. The office is at 206 Court Street in Chilton, keeps hours Monday through Friday from 8 am to 4:30 pm, and answers at (920) 849-1457. According to the county, the treasurer receives all county delinquent and postponed real estate taxes, takes the first installment for the City of New Holstein, settles the tax rolls with the towns, villages, cities and school districts, sends the delinquent notices and processes every property that becomes eligible for tax foreclosure.

A second job, the Real Property Lister, sits in the same office. Each time a property changes owners, a Transfer Form is recorded at the Register of Deeds. The recorded form then goes to the treasurer's office so the billing information on the parcel can change. The lister also builds the tax rolls for the municipal assessors, and the values from each assessor usually arrive between late February and late May.

sections.h2: What should a Calumet County home seller know about the county?
sections.html:
Calumet County is small, farm-heavy and bordered by water. It covers 397 square miles, but 79 of those are water, mostly Lake Winnebago along the western boundary. By land area it is the fifth-smallest county in Wisconsin.

Chilton is the county seat, and the county was organized in 1850. The 2020 census counted 52,442 residents, and the 2025 Census estimate is 53,982. The county sits inside the Appleton metropolitan area, and pieces of Appleton, Kaukauna and Menasha reach into its northwest corner. The southern end is known as the Holyland, settled in the 1840s by emigrants from the Schleswig-Holstein region of Germany. Earlier, in the 1830s, the Brothertown, Oneida and Stockbridge-Munsee peoples were relocated to the southwest part of the county.

Getting around is simple. No interstate crosses the county. U.S. 10 runs east to west along the northern edge, U.S. 151 runs near the western edge, Wisconsin 55 follows the western side, and Wisconsin 32/57 passes through the middle. The Niagara Escarpment runs north to south several miles east of Lake Winnebago, and glaciers shaped the rolling ground around it.

Farmland matters for taxes here. The county's tax bill guide explains that agricultural land is assessed on its ability to produce, so a farm parcel can show a zero estimated market value on the bill. A seller with acreage should read the bill closely before talking numbers with a buyer.

sections.h2: When are Calumet County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Full payment or the first installment is due January 31, and the second installment is due July 31. Local treasurers mail the real and personal property tax bills in early to mid December.

A bill over $100 can be split. The first half goes to the local treasurer by January 31, and the second half goes to the Calumet County Treasurer by July 31. The county's tax bill guide adds that the first installment must be paid in full and on time to keep the installment option. Personal property tax is paid to the local treasurer in full by January 31, unless the bill shows an installment option.

Mail needs a postmark on or before the due date, and a hand-delivered payment must reach the correct treasurer by that date. The county bill insert also says a payment received within five business days after the due date can still count as timely, a rule tied to Wisconsin Statute 74.69. Treat that as a safety net and pay early.

sections.h2: Which taxing districts appear on a Calumet County tax bill?
sections.html:
Up to five main districts can appear: the State of Wisconsin, Calumet County, a technical college, the municipality and a school district. Some parcels also sit inside a special district for a lake, sewer or fire protection, and that district takes a share too.

The county lists these local districts:

  • Towns: Brillion, Brothertown, Charlestown, Chilton, New Holstein, Rantoul, Stockbridge and Woodville.
  • Villages: Harrison, Hilbert, Potter, Sherwood and Stockbridge.
  • Cities: Brillion, Chilton and New Holstein, plus the Calumet County portions of Appleton, Kaukauna, Menasha and Kiel.
  • Technical colleges: Fox Valley, Moraine Park and Lakeshore.
  • School districts: Appleton, Brillion, Chilton, Hilbert, Kaukauna, Kiel, Kimberly, Menasha, New Holstein, Stockbridge and Wrightstown.

Two credits can reduce the bill. The first dollar credit goes to a property with a structure, whatever its use or value. The lottery and gaming credit goes to a property used as the owner's primary residence. The bill also shows an average assessment ratio for the municipality, which compares assessed values with the state's estimate of fair market value drawn from arm's length sales.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Calumet County assessment?
sections.html:
Your municipality's Board of Review hears the appeal. Calumet County assessors work for the individual town, village or city, so the board that hears your case sits in the place where the house stands.

Wisconsin Statute 70.47 sets the steps. The board meets during a 45-day window that begins on the fourth Monday of April, and the clerk must publish notice at least 15 days ahead (30 days in a year with a revaluation). The deadlines are tight:

  • Tell the board clerk, in writing or by phone, at least 48 hours before the first meeting that you plan to object.
  • File the written objection during the first two hours of that first meeting. The board can waive these steps for good cause or extraordinary circumstances.
  • Object to the combined value of land and improvements. An owner cannot challenge only the land or only the building.
  • State your own estimate of value in writing, with the information behind it, and be ready to testify under oath.

The board presumes the assessor's value is correct, and a tie vote leaves the assessment in place. Statute 70.47 also points to a claim for excessive assessment under Statute 74.37 for owners who go beyond the board. Ask the municipal clerk for the date of the next board meeting, because it changes each year.

sections.h2: What happens to a Calumet County house when taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The tax becomes delinquent, interest and penalty grow, and the county can eventually foreclose. Delinquent real property taxes are paid to the Calumet County Treasurer, while delinquent personal property taxes are paid to the local treasurer.

The charge is 1.5% per month from February 1, and notices go out in February and August. When a parcel reaches the stage where it is eligible for tax foreclosure, the treasurer processes it. The treasurer's page announced a property tax auction ending December 7, 2026 at 10:00 am, so an owner with a delinquent parcel should call the office before that date to learn where the parcel stands.

An owner who plans to sell has more options before foreclosure than after it. Getting a payoff figure early and settling the account at closing keeps the sale moving.

sections.h2: How do you sell a Calumet County house with tax due?
sections.html:
Get the exact balance from the treasurer, then settle it through closing. The balance depends on which installment has been paid, so the figure on last December's bill is only a starting point.

  • Call the Calumet County Treasurer at (920) 849-1457 and ask what is owed on the parcel, including any interest and penalty.
  • Ask whether the first installment went to the local treasurer and whether the second installment is still open for July 31.
  • Give the closing agent the parcel details so unpaid tax is paid from the sale proceeds.
  • Record the deed at the Register of Deeds with the electronic transfer return. Wisconsin charges the grantor a fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value or fraction under Statute 77.22(1), and the register collects it at recording.
  • After recording, the Real Property Lister updates the billing name and address on the parcel.

A house with a delinquent balance can still sell. The paperwork just needs the tax figure early, so the buyer's title work and the payoff line up.

faqs.q: When are Calumet County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due January 31 for full payment or the first installment, and July 31 for the second installment. The first goes to your local treasurer. The second goes to the Calumet County Treasurer in Chilton.

faqs.q: What interest does Calumet County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: The county states a rate of 1.5% per month, counted from February 1. The charge applies to a late first installment or a late second installment, and the unpaid tax is treated as delinquent.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of my Calumet County home?
faqs.a: A municipal assessor sets it. Each town, village and city contracts its own assessor, who sends values to the county's Real Property Lister, typically between late February and late May. The Wisconsin Department of Revenue separately estimates fair market value from arm's length sales for the bill.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Calumet County tax bill in two parts?
faqs.a: Yes, if the bill is over $100. Pay the first installment on time to your local treasurer by January 31 to keep the option, then pay the second to the county treasurer by July 31. Miss the first date and the installment option is lost.

faqs.q: Which credits lower a Calumet County tax bill?
faqs.a: The first dollar credit and the lottery and gaming credit. The first dollar credit applies to any property with a structure. The lottery and gaming credit applies to property used as the owner's primary residence.
